punchline: The gene-editing tool CRISPR began as curiosity about odd repeating DNA in bacteria.
thirty_sec: Microbiologists noticed strange repeating DNA in bacteria and did not know what it was for. It turned out to be a defence system: bacteria keep bits of virus DNA and use them to find and cut the same virus later. In 2012 Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier showed it could be steered to cut a chosen spot in DNA, and they shared the 2020 Nobel Prize. Walter Isaacson tells it in The Code Breaker.
